chunks.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ حَصَّانَ، الرَّازِيُّ، أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ. ضَعِيفٌ.

translations.en: Muhammad ibn Hassān, al-Rāzī, Abū Jaʿfar. Weak.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Duafa highlights Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān al-Rāzī, a narrator from the prominent Kufan school of hadith transmission. His classification as 'weak' (da'if) reflects the rigorous scrutiny applied by Shia scholars to ensure the authenticity of prophetic traditions, particularly regarding those who transmitted during the era of the Imams.
en.seo_question: Who is Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān al-Rāzī and what is his status in hadith sciences?

key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator is not considered fully reliable)
key_terms.الرَّازِيُّ: Al-Rāzī (a nisbah indicating origin from Ray, a city in Persia)
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar (a kunya, a teknonym meaning 'father of Jaʿfar')
